Custer-Terry June 21-22 Expedition Camp Site Custer June 23 and 24, 1976, Camp Sites
Most of these sites are located along the Yellowstone, Big Horn, and Little Big Horn Rivers, and Rosebud Creek: none are located on or near Tract II or Tract III.
A number of homestead sites are located within or adjacent to

Tracts II and III. None of these sites appears on or is being considered

for the National or State Antiquity registers, and it is unlikely that

any would be eligible for inclusion.
The Present Human Environment
The regional socio-economic base situation has been described in detail in a report prepared for Westmoreland Resources by Mountain West Reasearch, Inc. (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 c-f). This discussion focuses primarily on the area expected to experience the greatest socio-economic impact resulting from development of Tracts II and III.
The Area Impacted
At present the study area (hereafter referred to as the impact area) is rural with a population mix of Indian and non-Indian. Big Horn County, in which the major portion of the reservation lies, was 38.9 percent Indian in 1970, and the Crow Reservation proper was 56.1 percent Indian.
The Crow Indian Reservation lies 27 miles north of Sheridan,
Wyoming, and extends northerly and westerly to about 5 miles east of
Billings, Montana. These two cities (with 1970 populations of 10,856
and 71,197, respectively) provide many services not available in Big
